lines.en: It’s another night in Kumon-mi, which means-
Oh, good. Another perfectly timed phone call to distract me from whatever sad stuff is going on inside of my head and force me back into a state of conformational normalcy.
Good. I didn’t feel like narrating today anyway.
: Hello?
: Hello.
: Oh, Wakana. Is it time for our regularly scheduled unpaid therapy session again?
: Better. It’s time to get drunk.

: Sure. But let me warn you that if this is some sort of secret operation to make me so drunk that I confess to the many sins I’ve been hiding from you, it isn’t going to work. I know from experience.
: Yes, I’ve heard the stories. And no, that is not what is happening.
: I will still likely complain about things to you, though. I like the catharsis that comes from getting my frustrations out onto something that doesn’t involve proofreading.
: Yeah. Sadness starts feeling a lot less sad once you have to read over it and start correcting the spelling of stuff.
: Correct. But before you start heading to our regular bar, I’d like to warn you that I’m at the other one right now.
: The one I shan’t ever speak the name of out loud? That houses one of my greatest admirers and sometimes the covert agent of Satan that she created via human reproduction?
: Do not speak to me of human reproduction right now. I’m not in the mood.
: Oh no. Don’t tell me you’ve transitioned to full-on homosexuality. We haven’t even kissed yet.
: Sakaki-bar-a. Now.
Wakana hangs up the phone and I quickly start making my way over to [[REDACTED].
I also hold steady to that thing I said earlier about not wanting to narrate. Surprise. I’m here.
: Arakawa.
: Watabe.
: Sakakibara.
: Sorry. It didn’t seem like anyone else was going to say my name and I felt left out.
: I’ll take this box of clothes and go away now.
: Going through a goth phase, Sara?
: Me? No way. I tried that once in high school and there is just no way I have the time to maintain that aesthetic as an adult. These are for Sana.
: I just fear it might be a little too late as she isn’t as reserved as she was when we first talked about this exchange several years ago.
: Apologies for taking so long to bring you that box. I’ve just been so preoccupied by the time it takes to maintain this aesthetic as an adult.
: I’ll make sure she gets them. But don’t feel offended if you don’t see her wearing them any time soon. I can no longer control that girl and often feel as if she is the one controlling me now.
: Noted. I am perfectly content with never seeing your daughter again. So perhaps we just won’t cross paths at all and I will be none the wiser.
: Now, that’s just rude.
: Be gone, barmaid. You have overstayed your welcome and our transaction is over.
: Hey, you’re not looking for another job, are you? Because I could use another cool and mysterious woman now that my last one broke down.
: No. But if I ever give up on my career and dedicate the rest of my life to spiting my parents, I’ll be sure to let you know.
: I’ll take it. A win is a win in this economy. Need another drink? They’re on me tonight as thanks for the box of misery.
: Ten. And ten for my partner here as well.
: Partner?
: Partner.
: Sakakibara.
: I’ll see myself out now.
: So, you seem to have gotten a decently-sized head start. Maybe now I can finally manage to outlast you in the inebriation department.
: You likely will. My medication doesn’t react well with alcohol.
: I’d say you should probably stop drinking then. But I’m also not sure if it’s the same one you were taking when we had that foursome, and I don’t want to ruin my chances at a second one.
: It’s a different one.
: You should probably stop drinking then.
: This medication just winds up turning me on and then making me tired.
: Where is your bag? I’ll go get you some more.
: Heh. You would.
: Of course I would. You-
: You are smiling.
: I smile sometimes.
: But never after I make passes at you, so something must be seriously wrong.
: Care to take a guess?
: You have converted to full-on homosexuality. But it wasn’t until then that you realized your feelings for me and now it’s too late to go back.
: Arakawa, may I ask exactly what you see in me?
: Uhh...why?
: Curiosity, I suppose. You just make “passes” so often that there must be something about those feelings worth noting apart from me being extraordinarily attractive.
: I don’t know how to break this to you, but that’s really all it takes sometimes.
: But this is not one of those times as I know you well enough to know that you know me. So tell me — do you actually find me special? Or do you just say things like this for the fun of it?
: Well?
: Wakana, what’s going on? This is weird.
: I’m trying to find the words. It’s just difficult. And I thought hearing you ramble about how great I am would give me the time needed to come up with an explanation.
: Seems like that’s not in the cards either, though. And that my death-grip on life is loosening even quicker than Kafka’s battle with tuberculosis.
: Did...something happen with Osako?
: Yes.
: Something happened.
: I asked her to marry me.
: You...did? But...then why are you-
: Because she turned me down, obviously.
: How? Why? Osako’s more in love with you than anyone has ever been in love with anyone in the history of the universe. I don’t understand.
: I’m not sure how accurate that statement is given what I’ve heard about your childhood friend and her newfound interest in knife karate.
: I’m just going to ignore whatever it is you heard about that from Osako and say that Niki is probably just insane and that she doesn’t count.
: I think we’re probably all a little insane at the end of the day.
: So lost and confused that we can spend years of our lives right beside something or someone and just...completely overlook something so glaringly obvious.
: Perhaps it’s just an example of projection at play. Or believing in something because you want it to be true rather than ever actually thinking about it.
: And I have so much to think about all of a sudden. So much that the writer part of me is frothing at the mouth from the potential fruits of all of this.
: But the human part of me can’t help but be terrified of what branches may be snapped by plucking those fruits. I’m skeptical of their taste. Their texture. How it all feels.
: What an odd place to find myself in. So distraught, yet oddly excited about all that’s left to see.
: You guys...didn’t break up, did you? Because I know things haven’t been as perfect lately as they used to be, but-
: I don’t want children, Akira.
: Well...that’s great news then. Because I don’t know if you know this about human reproduction, which I know you warned me not to talk to you about, but two women-
: Osako does. Do you see what I’m saying?
: She wants something I never even noticed. Something that, after all this time, shook me to my core and took my breath away not out of love or admiration, but shock.
: I just...didn’t know. And what does that say about me? One half should know its other. And I just...didn’t.
: Well...maybe this is a new thing for her?
: Maybe something or...someone made her realize that not everything is impossible even when it seems like it is.
: Ah.
: So it was you who planted the seed.
: I obviously didn’t mean to. We were just talking about Ayane and then one thing led to another and-
: It’s fine. I don’t blame you.
: If anything, I should be thankful this happened now instead of another decade down the line after wasting so much of her time on this god-forsaken planet.
: Again, though — if this is a new thing, you shouldn’t beat yourself up about never realizing it. Things can still work out, can’t they? Maybe she...changes her mind?
: Things like this don’t come out of nowhere.
: I could spend days or weeks or months convincing myself that this is some sort of spontaneous urge or phase, but I know in my heart that all I’d be doing in thinking that is deceiving myself.
: I don’t want her to change her mind or settle for a life that’s less than perfect just to try and appease me. But again, I just...
: I don’t want children.
: It’s that simple...
: To think a single disagreement after so much time and love could amount to so much is just...
: It’s hard for me to understand.
: So no, I’m not doing okay.
: But, strangely enough, I don’t feel like crying.
: How curious, this numbness is. How unwanted. How sudden.
: How there are both good and bad sides to it.
: I think this is the end, Akira.
: I think the dream is finally over.
: That said, we should probably start charging one another if we’re going to keep doing this. What with unadulterated happiness apparently not being in the cards and all.
: You’ll find it one day, Wakana. There are very few people out there who deserve it more than you.
: I find it hard to believe that someone as selfish, obsessive, cynical, hostile, and overwhelmingly unpleasant as me could ever top the list of deserving anything worthwhile.
: As far as I’m concerned, all I’ve earned in all this time is exactly what I have given to others. Resentment. Exhaustion. Anguish.
: All these things and more make up the Wakana Watabe you’ve been duped into befriending. And sooner or later, you’ll find that I’m nothing but a road to nowhere as well.
: Hey. There’s only enough room for one self-deprecating asshole in this friend group and that asshole is me.
: And yes, you might be selfish, obsessive, cynical, hostile, and overwhelmingly unpleasant — but you’re also creative, hot, artistic, hot, eccentric, and really fucking hot.
: That was basically just two adjectives. I actually feel even worse about myself now if that’s the best you can come up with.
: I’m sure you do. But, on the bright side, this is probably the single lowest moment of your life so far. So you can take solace in knowing things can only go up from here.
: And that you’ll have an equally selfish, obsessive, cynical, hostile, and overwhelmingly unpleasant person beside you the whole way.
: You don’t know that for sure. We haven’t seen what this will do to our group yet. For all we know, everything could fall apart and the two of us could wind up completely alone.
: Then let’s make a promise that you and I won’t ever fall out of touch even if that happens.
: I don’t want to do that either, though. You’re even worse than me and I reserve the right to cut you off at any moment I find beneficial.
: Okay, fine. Then I promise to not stop bothering you until that happens. You deserve at least one constant while everything else is changing. Okay?
: Okay?
: You know...
: You’re really impressive in a lot of really unpredictable ways sometimes.
: Am I? How?
: Just that you’ve done this multiple times before — lost someone who meant the world to you. And you’re still standing and telling me to go on while struggling to do the same yourself.
: Oh, yeah. That’s just one of the very few examples out there of hypocrisy being a net positive.
: It’s just a little admirable is all. I still think you’re a terrible, undesirable person who deserves all of the pain he routinely receives.
: And you are well within your right to think those things. But it changes nothing and I’m still here.
: You are...
: Aren’t you?
: I am.
: But there’s one thing I should probably tell you before this goes any further.
: Oh, joy. I’ve been waiting for the second shoe to drop for some time now. Walking around with one has been rather painful.
: Wakana, if we’re going to keep being friends, I need you to know...
: That I also want kids.
: Please laugh. That was funny.
: Hilarious.
: Too soon?
: Too soon.
: Got it. No more Osako jokes until I receive permission. See? I can be a good friend.
: You can, yes. When you actually want to be. I just wish that were more often.
: Be careful what you wish for, Wakana. Saying things like that is only going to make me more annoying.
: Can it wait a few minutes while I rest my head on your shoulder? Right on cue, my self-medication cocktail is making me tired again.
: Sure, but...
: Just out of curiosity, has that other side effect you mentioned kicked in yet?
: What other side effect?
: You said the medication turns you on and then makes you tired.
: I don’t remember saying that. You’re making things up.
: That...might be true. But I could have sworn-
: No more words. Just let me rest and feel sorry for myself a little while longer.
: Fine. But I will not allow you to police anything that goes on in my head while that happens.
: I’d say it’s probably best if we just stay out of each other’s heads entirely. I’m not sure you’re ready for what goes on inside of mine yet.
: What is that supposed to-
: Goodnight, Arakawa. Wake me up in...ten minutes? Twenty maybe, if I look particularly peaceful.
: Can I keep my arm around you at least?
: Just this once. But only because I don’t have the energy to fight back.
: I will do my best to...not keep that in mind.
Wakana drifts off to sleep on my shoulder.
I wake her up twenty minutes later.
There is no more narration.
Wakana’s affection has increased to [wakana_love]!
You’ve received a new picture message from Rika Rokuhara!
